name: IA-04
label: Likely R

key_factors: District's R+15 partisan lean strongly favors Republicans holding the open seat
McGowan holds a large fundraising edge: $444k cash on hand versus $42k for Dawson
Prediction markets price a Democratic win at only a few percent
No public polling or expert ratings, and an open seat adds uncertainty
model.rationale: The district's fifteen-point Republican lean, Chris McGowan's decisive financial advantage over David Dawson, and market pricing near 96% Republican all point to the seat staying in GOP hands despite Feenstra's retirement; the absence of any polling keeps uncertainty wider than in a typical safe seat.
model.watch: A nationalized Democratic environment or a poorly funded, divisive Republican general-election campaign could narrow what is otherwise a comfortable Republican margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Randy Feenstra (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Northwest Iowa's 4th District is one of the most Republican seats in the state, and Randy Feenstra's retirement to run for governor leaves the open seat with a Republican nominee who starts with every structural advantage. Chris McGowan has raised more than $860,000 and holds a large cash lead over Democrat David Dawson, who has about $42,000 on hand. Outside groups have spent modestly to support McGowan and nothing to oppose him.

No public polls cover the race and no expert raters have weighed in, so the forecast rests on fundamentals and prediction markets, which price a Democratic win at only a few percent. The district's fifteen-point Republican lean and the GOP's money edge make an upset possible but unlikely. The real question is the size of the margin, though an open seat without polling always carries some uncertainty.
